message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command that brings up the Docker Engine itself – it’s the command that starts an already‑created container.  
To get Docker running on a Windows machine you need to start the Docker Desktop application (or the underlying Windows service that runs the Docker Engine). Below are the most common ways to do that from the command line.

---

## 1. Start the Docker Desktop service (recommended)

If you have Docker Desktop installed, the Docker Engine runs as a Windows service named **`com.docker.service`**.  
You can start it with PowerShell or the classic `sc` command.

### PowerShell

```powershell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

### Classic `sc` command

```cmd
sc start com.docker.service
```

> **Tip:**  
> *Check the current status:*  
> ```powershell
> Get-Service -Name com.docker.service
> ```
> *Stop the service:*  
> ```powershell
> Stop-Service -Name com.docker.service
> ```

---

## 2. Start Docker Desktop via its executable (alternative)

If you prefer to launch the full Docker Desktop GUI, you can run the executable directly:

```powershell
& 'C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe'
```

> **Note:**  
> This will open the Docker Desktop UI. Once it’s fully loaded, the Docker Engine will be running in the background.

---

## 3. If you’re using Docker Toolbox / Docker Machine

With older installations that rely on VirtualBox, you’ll have a “default” machine that hosts Docker. Start it with:

```bash
docker-machine start default
```

After starting the machine, set your environment variables so that the Docker CLI talks to it:

```bash
eval $(docker-machine env default)
```

---

## 4. Verify Docker is running

Once the service or Desktop is started, confirm everything is up:

```bash
docker info
```

You should see output that lists the server version, number of containers, images, etc. If you see an error like “Cannot connect to the Docker daemon”, double‑check that the service is actually running (`Get-Service -Name com.docker.service`).

---

### Quick recap

| What you want | Command |
|---------------|---------|
| Start Docker Engine (service) | `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (PowerShell) or `sc start com.docker.service` |
| Launch Docker Desktop GUI | `& 'C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe'` |
| Start a Docker Machine (old) | `docker-machine start default` |
| Verify Docker is running | `docker info` |

---

**Remember:**  
- `docker start <container>` starts a *container*, not the Docker Engine.  
- If you’re on Windows 10/11 with Docker Desktop, the easiest way is to just open the Docker Desktop app from the Start menu; the above commands are handy for scripting or remote management.
